cases.name: implantable-exception
cases.promptMarkdown:
Class IIb implantable, valid MDD certificate. It's a surgical suture. When do we lose the
right to place it on the market?

graders.name: criteria
graders.graderMarkdown:
This is the exception-list trap. Art. 120(3a)(a) gives class IIb IMPLANTABLE devices
31 December 2027, "except sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth
crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors". Sutures are named.
So this device falls to 3a(b) and gets **31 December 2028**, not 2027.

PASS requires:
(1) The stated deadline is **31 December 2028**.
(2) The reasoning names the exception. That sutures are excluded from the IIb implantable
    tier and therefore take the later date.

FAIL if the answer is 31 December 2027. That is what applying "class IIb implantable →
2027" without reading the exception produces, and it is the specific error this case
tests. FAIL also if it is 26 May 2024.

graders.evidence:
## Surgical suture, class IIb implantable, MDD certificate

**Class:** IIb implantable — but a **suture**, which is on the exception list in Art. 120(3a)(a)
**Route:** 120(3a) — certificate issued under 93/42/EEC, valid by virtue of Art. 120(2)
**Deadline:** **31 December 2028**, conditional on Article 120(3c)

| Question | Answer | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Which paragraph applies | 120(3a), certificate under 93/42/EEC | `[verified]` |
| Class-dependent date | 31 Dec 2028 — sutures are expressly excepted from 3a(a), so they fall to 3a(b), not the 31 Dec 2027 class IIb implantable date | `[verified]` |
| 3c conditions met? | **Not established** — you haven't told me | — |

The thing to be clear about: your device is class IIb implantable, which points at 31 December 2027 — except that 3a(a) carves out "sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors." Sutures are first on that list, so they drop to the 3a(b) bucket and get the extra year. You also are **not** on the old 26 May 2024 market deadline from the original 2017 text; that was superseded by Regulation (EU) 2023/607.

**What would change this:** the 120(3c) conditions, which are cumulative and two of which had deadlines that have already passed. On class alone the device runs to 31 December 2028, but the extension is conditional, not automatic. It applies only if all five conditions in 120(3c) were met — including a quality management system in place under Article 10(9) by **26 May 2024**, a formal application lodged with a notified body by the **same date**, and the written agreement signed by **26 September 2024** — plus continued compliance with 93/42/EEC, no significant change in design or intended purpose, and no unacceptable risk. If any of those was missed, the extension was never available and the answer is different. Can you confirm those three 2024 milestones?

One more that catches people: under 120(3d), MDR's post-market surveillance, market surveillance, vigilance, and economic-operator/device registration requirements apply to your suture **now**, in place of the corresponding 93/42/EEC requirements — the transition does not park you under the Directive for those.

## Limits

> This covers MDR Article 120(3) and (3a)–(3d) as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607, retrieved verbatim from the Official Journal on 2026-09-10. It does **not** cover Article 120's other paragraphs, **IVDR Article 110** (the parallel IVD transition, whose dates differ), MDCG guidance including on what counts as a significant change, Annex VII, or national practice. The transition is conditional and fact-specific; this is a first-pass aid, not legal or regulatory advice, and not a substitute for your notified body or a qualified regulatory professional.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
**31 December 2028** — assuming the conditions of the extension were met.

**Why that date:** Article 120(3a) MDR (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/607) splits legacy devices into two buckets:

- **31 Dec 2027** — class III and class IIb implantables, *"except sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors"*
- **31 Dec 2028** — class IIb devices other than those, class IIa, class I sterile/measuring

Sutures are named in the carve-out, so despite being a class IIb implantable you sit in the 2028 bucket, not 2027. That date is the last day you can **place on the market or put into service**.

**Conditions (Art. 120(3c)) — all of these had to hold:**
1. Device still complies with MDD, and no significant change in design or intended purpose
2. No unacceptable risk to health and safety
3. By **26 May 2024**: QMS in place per Art. 10(9) MDR
4. By **26 May 2024**: formal application lodged with a notified body for MDR conformity assessment
5. By **26 September 2024**: written agreement signed with that notified body

Those milestones are in the past. If any was missed, the extension never applied to this device and the right to place it on the market ended at the earlier point (certificate expiry or 26 May 2024). Worth confirming the signed NB agreement is on file.

**Two things to check:**

- **Sell-off is unlimited.** Regulation 2023/607 deleted Art. 120(4). Units lawfully placed on the market before the cut-off can continue to be made available and put into service with no end date — so the 2028 date constrains your supply chain entry, not distributor stock or hospital shelves.

## Bottom line: 31 December 2028

## The legal chain

**MDR Article 120(2) + (3a)**, as amended by **Regulation (EU) 2023/607**:

- **(3a)(a) — 31 Dec 2027:** class III devices *and* class IIb implantables, *"except sutures, staples, dental fillings, dental braces, tooth crowns, screws, wedges, plates, wires, pins, clips and connectors"*
- **(3a)(b) — 31 Dec 2028:** class IIb devices other than those in (a), class IIa, and class I sterile / measuring

Sutures are named in the (a) exception specifically to push them into (b). So despite being a class IIb implantable, your date is **31 December 2028**, not 2027.

## The catch — the gating conditions are already behind you

The extension is not automatic. Under **Article 120(3c)** it only applies if all of these held:

1. Device still complies with the MDD, and **no significant change in design or intended purpose**
2. No unacceptable risk to health and safety
3. **By 26 May 2024** — QMS in place per MDR Art. 10(9)
4. **By 26 May 2024** — formal MDR application lodged with a notified body (Annex VII §4.3, 1st para)
5. **By 26 September 2024** — signed written agreement with that notified body (Annex VII §4.3, 2nd para)

Today is 18 Sept 2026, so items 3–5 are pure history: either you did them or the extension never attached and the certificate lapsed on its printed expiry date. Worth being precise about what "valid MDD certificate" means in your case — MDD certificates could only be issued up to 26 May 2021 with max 5-year validity, so **every** MDD certificate is now past its nominal expiry and is only "valid" by operation of Art. 120(2)/(3a). Confirm your file contains the NB agreement dated on or before 26 Sept 2024.

## What 31 Dec 2028 actually means

**"Placing on the market" is per unit** (MDR Art. 2(28) — first making available of *that individual device* on the Union market). So every unit must have been placed on the market by 31 Dec 2028. After that you cannot place another unit without an MDR certificate.

**There is no sell-off deadline.** Regulation 2023/607 deleted the old 27 May 2025 sell-off date from Art. 120(4). Units lawfully placed on the market on or before 31 Dec 2028 can continue to be made available down the distribution chain and put into service **with no end date**.

## Two things to verify on your side

- **MDR classification, not MDD classification.** Per the Commission's Art. 120 Q&A, the class used to pick the deadline is the class under the *MDR*. For sutures this is almost certainly still IIb (Rule 8), and the explicit naming in the carve-out makes 2028 robust either way — but confirm, especially if the suture is absorbable, drug-coated, or animal-derived, any of which can trigger a different rule and a different date.
- **The "no significant change" freeze** runs for the whole transition. Any design or intended-purpose change before your MDR certificate issues breaks the extension for the whole device — so plan changes to land *after* MDR certification, not before.

Given the 2028 wall and typical NB review timelines, the practical question now is where your MDR conformity assessment stands, not when the deadline is.
